newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1996 c/a deficit seen at 8.0-8.5 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1996 c/a deficit seen at 8.0-8.5 pct of GDP.

text.p: The Thai current account deficit would likely be 8.0-8.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1996 against 8.1 percent in 1995, an economist at the National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) said on Tuesday.
The economist said the six-year high deficit, compared with 8.5 percent posted in 1990, is expected despite a slowing economy and sluggish exports this year.
He said GDP would likely expand in a 7.0-7.5 percent range this year against 7.8 percent projected by the Bank of Thailand in late July and 8.6 percent in 1995.
The economist at NESDB, Thailand's official long-term economic think tank, said exports could post nearly five percent growth for 1996.
Exports slowed sharply this year from 1995 when they registered a 23.5 percent increase.
The economist also said 1996 inflation would not ease below last year's 5.8 percent, partly due to higher food prices induced by floods over the past two months.
He said the consumer price index would likely range between 5.8-6.0 percent this year.
